description: A privacy-conscious Telegram bot with phone-number registration, per-document UZS pricing, payment-proof review, user-specific document delivery, and admin commands in the same bot.

services.name: Telegram bot and admin commands
services.description: A Telegram bot that handles user registration, text and image submissions, paid Word generation, private user requests, receipt review, and restricted administrator commands. The admin panel is part of this same bot; no separate web frontend is requested.

questions.question: Which programming language should the Telegram bot use?

options.label: Python
options.description: Matches the existing bot.py project and its current Python Telegram library.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use a TypeScript-based Telegram bot implementation.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use a JavaScript-based Telegram bot implementation.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Use a .NET-based Telegram bot implementation.

questions.rationale: The workspace contains an existing Python Telegram bot and the request asks to reuse the same bot.

questions.question: Which framework should handle Telegram updates and bot commands?

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Use an Azure Functions-based webhook implementation.

questions.rationale: The existing bot uses python-telegram-bot polling. Retaining it avoids silently replacing the requested existing bot framework; Azure Functions is available as an alternative.

questions.question: What should the bot do? Review or add requirements, especially how submitted text and photos become Word documents, the commands for users/admins, and any existing bot behavior that must be retained.
questions.recommendedChoice: Phone-number registration and verification; after /start show available commands and warn that each generated Word file costs 5,000 UZS; users submit text and images privately; users request and receive only their own generated Word files by command; purchase command shows an admin-configured card number and requests payment proof; receipt photos go to an admin review group with approve/reject buttons; allow a mistaken decision to be reversed within five minutes; authorized admins can inspect users and their submitted text, images, and generated files; store content privately and deliver it only to its owner on request.
questions.answer: Phone-number registration and verification; after /start show available commands and warn that each generated Word file costs 5,000 UZS; users submit text and images privately; users request and receive only their own generated Word files by command; purchase command shows an admin-configured card number and requests payment proof; receipt photos go to an admin review group with approve/reject buttons; allow a mistaken decision to be reversed within five minutes; authorized admins can inspect users and their submitted text, images, and generated files; store content privately and deliver it only to its owner on request.
questions.rationale: These behaviors are directly specified. The document-generation inputs and details of command flows remain to be confirmed in the product questions below.

questions.question: Which data stores should the project use?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Only suitable if the application does not persist users, submissions, payment reviews, generated files, or other data.

options.label: Azure Database for PostgreSQL
options.description: Store user profiles, registration state, payment/review records, ownership metadata, and audit history.

options.label: Azure SQL Database
options.description: Relational database alternative for user, payment, and ownership metadata.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Private object storage for submitted images, text attachments if applicable, payment proofs, and generated Word files.

options.label: Azure Queue Storage
options.description: Optional queue for asynchronous document generation or review tasks.

options.label: Azure Cache for Redis
options.description: Optional cache for short-lived state or frequently accessed data.

questions.rationale: Persisted user/payment/ownership records and private files are required. The database product is not specified; PostgreSQL is a suggested default. Blob Storage is required for images and generated Word files.

questions.question: Should users register and verify their phone number before using the bot's application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require phone-number registration and verification before allowing protected bot features.

options.label: No
options.description: Do not require users to sign in or verify a phone number.

questions.rationale: The request explicitly requires phone-number registration and verification.

questions.question: How should the bot verify a user's phone number?
questions.recommendedChoice: Ask the user to share their Telegram contact and verify it belongs to the current Telegram account

options.label: Telegram shared contact
options.description: Request the user's contact using Telegram's contact-sharing flow and confirm it is their own contact.

options.label: SMS one-time code
options.description: Send an OTP by SMS; requires an SMS provider and additional cost.

options.label: Admin verification
options.description: Collect a phone number and require an administrator to verify it manually.

questions.answer: Ask the user to share their Telegram contact and verify it belongs to the current Telegram account
questions.rationale: Phone verification is required, but the verification method was not specified.

questions.question: Where should the continuously running Telegram bot be hosted on Azure?

options.label: Azure Container Apps
options.description: Run the existing polling bot as a managed container/worker.

options.label: Azure App Service
options.description: Host a continuously running bot process with an appropriate always-on configuration.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Use a webhook-oriented event-driven implementation instead of the existing polling process.

options.label: Not decided
options.description: Defer hosting selection until architecture planning.

questions.rationale: The existing bot uses long polling and is a background worker; a managed container is a plausible Azure fit, but hosting is unspecified.

questions.question: Which Telegram accounts should be allowed to use admin commands and view user content?
questions.recommendedChoice: A configured allowlist of one or more Telegram user IDs, with one primary administrator

options.label: One primary administrator
options.description: Only one configured Telegram user ID can administer the bot.

options.label: Allowlisted administrators
options.description: One or more explicitly configured Telegram user IDs can administer the bot.

options.label: Role-based administrators
options.description: Support multiple administrator roles with separately scoped permissions.

questions.answer: A configured allowlist of one or more Telegram user IDs, with one primary administrator
questions.rationale: The existing code supports ADMIN_IDS, while the request does not specify whether there is one admin or multiple administrators. Admin access to private user content should be explicitly restricted.

questions.question: How should the receipt-review Telegram group be configured?
questions.recommendedChoice: An administrator configures the Telegram group ID through a protected setting; do not place a real group ID in this planning file

options.label: Protected configuration
options.description: Store the group ID in a protected deployment setting and restrict access to configured administrators.

options.label: Configure through admin commands
options.description: An authorized administrator sets or changes the review group from the bot.

options.label: No group; review in private admin chat
options.description: Send payment proofs and approval controls to an authorized administrator's private chat.

questions.answer: An administrator configures the Telegram group ID through a protected setting; do not place a real group ID in this planning file
questions.rationale: A review group is requested, but its administration/configuration method is unspecified. Do not collect actual identifiers or payment details in this plan.

questions.question: How should an administrator enter and update the card number shown by the purchase command?
questions.recommendedChoice: Set or update it through a restricted admin command, with the value stored in protected configuration and never echoed in logs

options.label: Restricted admin command
options.description: An authorized admin configures the displayed card number in the bot; protect access and avoid logging the value.

options.label: Deployment secret/configuration
options.description: An operator updates a protected Azure setting outside Telegram.

options.label: Both
options.description: Support an initial protected setting and controlled admin updates.

questions.answer: Set or update it through a restricted admin command, with the value stored in protected configuration and never echoed in logs
questions.rationale: The card number is to be entered by an admin, but the setting workflow is not specified. The actual card number must not be included in this requirements file.

questions.question: How should submitted text and images be used to generate Word files?
questions.recommendedChoice: Use a defined document template and collect the required text/images through guided bot commands

options.label: Guided bot form and fixed template
options.description: Collect specified fields and photos through commands, then generate a Word file from a fixed template.

options.label: User-uploaded Word template
options.description: Allow each user to submit a Word template and populate it with their content.

options.label: Free-form text and images
options.description: Accept content and images, then create a document using a general layout.

options.label: Preserve current workflow
options.description: Adapt the existing bot's school/class, student-name, photo, and Word-template workflow.

questions.rationale: The workspace bot currently processes school/class data, names, photos, and a Word template, but the requested new bot's intended document input format is not specified.

questions.question: How should the 5,000 UZS price and purchases be applied?
questions.recommendedChoice: Manual proof review grants one document-generation credit per approved payment; charge 5,000 UZS per generated Word file

options.label: One credit per approved payment
options.description: Each 5,000 UZS approved payment grants exactly one Word generation.

options.label: Admin-entered package quantities
options.description: Admins define packages and prices; the specified 5,000 UZS per Word remains the unit price.

options.label: Generate first, then reconcile manually
options.description: Allow generation before payment confirmation and track outstanding payment manually.

questions.answer: Manual proof review grants one document-generation credit per approved payment; charge 5,000 UZS per generated Word file
questions.rationale: The per-file price and proof review are specified, but the number of files per payment and credit/refund behavior are not.

questions.question: How long should submitted text, photos, payment proofs, and generated Word files be retained?
questions.recommendedChoice: Retain only as long as needed for the user's service and payment/audit requirements; provide an admin-controlled deletion policy and define a retention period before launch

options.label: Until user requests deletion
options.description: Keep data until an authorized deletion request, subject to legally required payment records.

options.label: Fixed retention period
options.description: Automatically delete content after a defined period; enter the period as a follow-up.

options.label: Keep generated files; delete source uploads
options.description: Retain only the generated Word file after a defined processing/verification period.

questions.answer: Retain only as long as needed for the user's service and payment/audit requirements; provide an admin-controlled deletion policy and define a retention period before launch
questions.rationale: The request requires private handling and admin visibility, but does not state retention or deletion rules. Files should be private, owner-scoped for user retrieval, and accessible only to authorized admins.
